title: P66 (Papyrus Bodmer II): John 17:1-18:3 (pages 121-125)
source: Papyrus Bodmer II (P66), Fondation Martin Bodmer: images from the Bodmer Lab, University of Geneva; Greek from the INTF NTVMR transcription of P66; English from the King James Version
description: John 17:1-18:3 in P66 (Papyrus Bodmer II), the papyrus codex of John copied around 200: pages 121-125, each with its photograph, the Greek transcription and the King James Version.
introduction:
P66 is a papyrus codex of the Gospel of John copied in Egypt around 200, the most complete early copy of John. Most of it is Papyrus Bodmer II in the Fondation Martin Bodmer, Cologny (Geneva); small pieces are in the Chester Beatty Library, Dublin, and the Institut für Altertumskunde, Cologne. The first five quires (John 1:1-14:26) survive as a bound book of numbered pages; later leaves, from John 14:29 to 21:9, are damaged and kept between glass. The scribe made many corrections, some of them his own; only the first hand is shown here.

Each section below is one page: the photograph, the NTVMR diplomatic transcription line by line, and the King James Version of every verse on the page. Pages of the bound book are shown on the photographic plates published by Victor Martin and J. W. B. Barns in 1962 (scanned by the Bodmer Lab), the glass-mounted leaves on colour photographs. Lost: John 6:12-34 (pages 35-38) and parts of chapters 14-21; the transcription ends at 21:9. Where P66 lacks a verse that the KJV has (John 5:4, the account of the adulteress at 7:53-8:11, 16:15), the section says so.

This entry covers pages 121-125 (John 17:1-18:3).
translator_notes: Greek: the NTVMR diplomatic transcription, line by line as on the papyrus. Square brackets enclose letters that are lost or illegible and were supplied by the transcribers; a dot under a letter marks it as uncertain; [...] marks a gap. Nomina sacra and numerals keep the scribe's overline. Spelling is the scribe's (no accents or breathings). Words broken at a line end stay broken as on the papyrus. Corrections are not shown: the text is the first hand.

English: the King James Version (1611), whole verses, for every verse that has text on the page. A verse that begins on one page and ends on the next is given in full on both. The KJV translates a later form of the Greek text, so its wording does not always match the papyrus; material differences (such as verses the papyrus does not have) are noted in the section.

translation.text: <sup>17:1</sup>These words spake Jesus, and lifted up his eyes to heaven, and said, Father, the hour is come; glorify thy Son, that thy Son also may glorify thee: <sup>2</sup>As thou hast given him power over all flesh, that he should give eternal life to as many as thou hast given him. <sup>3</sup>And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent. <sup>4</sup>I have glorified thee on the earth: I have finished the work which thou gavest me to do. <sup>5</sup>And now, O Father, glorify thou me with thine own self with the glory which I had with thee before the world was. <sup>6</sup>I have manifested thy name unto the men which thou gavest me out of the world: thine they were, and thou gavest them me; and they have kept thy word. <sup>7</sup>Now they have known that all things whatsoever thou hast given me are of thee.
translation.scan_note: Fondation Martin Bodmer, Papyrus Bodmer II, Bodmer Lab image 1072205287_125 (https://bodmerlab.unige.ch/fr/constellations/papyri/mirador/1072205287), colour photograph of the glass-mounted leaf, shown whole. NTVMR page 1170 (page 121) is linked to this image in NTVMR's page index. 17:1 begins on the previous page; 17:7 continues on the next page. Checked on the image: the printed caption reads ‹PB II Evangile de Jean, supplément 17, 1-7›.

translation.text: <sup>17:8</sup>For I have given unto them the words which thou gavest me; and they have received them, and have known surely that I came out from thee, and they have believed that thou didst send me. <sup>9</sup>I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me; for they are thine. <sup>10</sup>And all mine are thine, and thine are mine; and I am glorified in them. <sup>11</sup>And now I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me, that they may be one, as we are. <sup>12</sup>While I was with them in the world, I kept them in thy name: those that thou gavest me I have kept, and none of them is lost, but the son of perdition; that the scripture might be fulfilled.

translation.text: <sup>17:13</sup>And now come I to thee; and these things I speak in the world, that they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves. <sup>14</sup>I have given them thy word; and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world. <sup>15</sup>I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil. <sup>16</sup>They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world. <sup>17</sup>Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth. <sup>18</sup>As thou hast sent me into the world, even so have I also sent them into the world. <sup>19</sup>And for their sakes I sanctify myself, that they also might be sanctified through the truth.

translation.text: <sup>17:20</sup>Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word; <sup>21</sup>That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us: that the world may believe that thou hast sent me. <sup>22</sup>And the glory which thou gavest me I have given them; that they may be one, even as we are one: <sup>23</sup>I in them, and thou in me, that they may be made perfect in one; and that the world may know that thou hast sent me, and hast loved them, as thou hast loved me. <sup>24</sup>Father, I will that they also, whom thou hast given me, be with me where I am; that they may behold my glory, which thou hast given me: for thou lovedst me before the foundation of the world.

translation.text: <sup>17:25</sup>O righteous Father, the world hath not known thee: but I have known thee, and these have known that thou hast sent me. <sup>26</sup>And I have declared unto them thy name, and will declare it: that the love wherewith thou hast loved me may be in them, and I in them. <sup>18:1</sup>When Jesus had spoken these words, he went forth with his disciples over the brook Cedron, where was a garden, into the which he entered, and his disciples. <sup>2</sup>And Judas also, which betrayed him, knew the place: for Jesus ofttimes resorted thither with his disciples. <sup>3</sup>Judas then, having received a band of men and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees, cometh thither with lanterns and torches and weapons.
